credit.rationale: Reaffirmed (Credit Bulletin dated 02-Jul-2026). Ratings continue to reflect RPL's established market position in IT and peripheral products distribution, improving product and geographical diversification in revenue, strong risk management practices, and healthy financial risk profile; partially offset by modest (though improving) operating margin and large working-capital requirement. Crisil took note of RPL's 23-Jun-2026 announcement of acquiring a 67% stake in VDA Infosolutions Pvt Ltd (rated Crisil BBB+/Watch Positive) for Rs 368.50 cr, with a plan to acquire 100% in a staggered manner by H1 fiscal 2029; VDA's revenues are ~5% of group revenues.

bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic investment made in VDA Infosolutions, described by the deck as "a significant step towards forward integration and expanding capabilities in managed IT services, solution implementation, and lifecycle support"; stake size and consideration are not disclosed.
- Net Debt to Equity of 0.35x (FY24), 0.50x (FY25) and 0.43x (FY26); the glance page repeats 0.43 as the FY26 figure.
- Returns disclosed as RoCE of 12.93% (FY24), 13.02% (FY25) and 16.02% (FY26), and RoE of 12.79% (FY24), 12.74% (FY25) and 14.74% (FY26).
- Cash flow from operations was negative in the growth years and turned positive in FY26: INR -1,020 mn (FY24), -2,992 mn (FY25) and 1,137 mn (FY26) — consistent with the balance sheet's build in inventories (INR 14,934 mn in FY23 to 25,537 mn in FY26) and trade receivables (INR 8,716 mn to 21,842 mn over the same period).
- Balance sheet is funded largely by short-term working-capital debt: current borrowings of INR 9,586 mn in FY26 against nil non-current borrowings, with total equity of INR 20,363 mn.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified portfolio of 18,400+ SKUs spanning personal computing, enterprise infrastructure, components, storage, networking, lifestyle and emerging technology, enabling multi-segment participation across consumer, SMB and enterprise customers.
- Long-standing brand relationships: of 78 global technology brands represented, 23 brands associated for over 5 years contribute 88% of revenue, and 11 brands with relationships exceeding 10 years contribute 72% of revenue.
- One of India's largest ICT distribution ecosystems — 55 branches, 71 warehouses and presence across 700+ locations, serving 10,300+ partners and B2B customers across general trade, modern trade and e-commerce.
- Early mover in semiconductor distribution — first ICT distributor in India to enter the segment (2021) — supported by a dedicated Embedded Lab in Bengaluru.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Technology obsolescence — Identified by the Risk Management Committee as a primary risk area for an ICT distributor whose SKU portfolio is exposed to rapid product-cycle change.
- Cybersecurity threats — Flagged both in the Risk Management framework and separately by the Board, which noted the Company 'remains vigilant in addressing evolving cyber security threats to its IT systems', with Internal Audit monitoring control effectiveness across all locations.
- Supply chain disruptions — A distribution business is directly exposed to disruption in the global technology supply chain feeding its inventory.
- Component price volatility — Named as a distinct risk the Risk Management Committee monitors, relevant given the Company's dependence on globally-sourced ICT components and hardware.
- Customer demand fluctuations — Demand volatility across the Company's General Trade, Modern Trade and E-Commerce customer base is explicitly tracked as a risk factor.
- Market competitiveness — Competitive intensity in ICT distribution is monitored as a structural risk to market share and margins.
- Regulatory changes — Changes in applicable regulation are tracked as a risk given the Company's compliance obligations across corporate, tax and listing regulations.
- Working capital management and credit risk — Distribution requires significant investment in inventory and receivables; the Risk Management Committee explicitly monitors working-capital management and credit risk as core operating risks.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Evolve from a distribution business into a broader technology solutions partner, resting on three priorities: strengthening the core personal computing/enterprise/components engine, developing higher-margin higher-growth verticals with semiconductors at the centre, and pursuing margin expansion by integrating across the value chain into solutions and services.
- For FY2027: strengthen the core, develop higher-return verticals (semiconductors, data centres, AI, software & cybersecurity, managed services) that will shape the next decade, and expand capabilities across the value chain.
- Grow the semiconductor vertical further — first ICT distributor in India to enter the segment (2021), supported by a dedicated Embedded Lab in Bengaluru, with new semiconductor subsidiaries in India and Singapore strengthening dedicated operations.
- Deepen presence in smaller (Tier-2/Tier-3) cities via branch network expansion, and broaden the brand portfolio through new partnerships across enterprise, education technology and premium consumer devices.
- Position the Company as a partner in India's AI adoption (not only a hardware supplier) through structured AI Bootcamps and developer/enterprise engagement.
- Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 2 per equity share of Rs. 5 face value (40%) for FY2025-26, to be declared at the 37th AGM (September 9, 2026), governed by the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy under SEBI Listing Regulation 43A.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: As an asset-light ICT distributor (no manufacturing plants; BRSR discloses 0 plants and 70 domestic + 1 international office/branch locations), RP tech's 'expansion' is footprint and vertical build-out rather than physical capacity. During FY26 the Company added three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur), taking its branch network to 55 branches (71 warehouses, 700+ locations), deepening Tier-II/Tier-III presence. It strengthened its semiconductor and embedded vertical through its Bengaluru Embedded Lab (reference-design, board bring-up, PCB design and AI/ML application development) and by incorporating new semiconductor subsidiaries in India (Rashi Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited) and, after the FY26 close (post 1 April 2026), a Singapore step-down subsidiary (Rashi Semiconductor Solutions Pte Ltd, 100% held by the Indian semiconductor subsidiary) and a Dubai step-down subsidiary (Rashi Peripherals LLC-FZ, 98% held by Rashi Peripherals Pte Ltd, Singapore). It also incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary, RP Tech Electronics Limited. Subsequent to year-end, the Board (June 23, 2026) approved and completed (July 2, 2026) the acquisition of 67% of VDA Infosolutions Private Limited for Rs 368.50 crore cash, with the remaining 33% stake to be acquired over the next three years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- AI PC transition (NPU-equipped devices, Copilot+ PC platform, Windows 10 end-of-support) is driving a multi-year upgrade cycle and robust demand for GPUs, AI-enabled processors, memory modules, SSDs, cooling and power-management solutions.
- Enterprise refresh cycle: replacement of ageing devices and migration to AI-ready systems is accelerating commercial PC upgrades; India enterprise segment and workstation shipments grew strongly in Q1 2026.
- Data-centre build-out in India (installed capacity ~1.9 GW in FY26, more than doubling from ~778 MW in FY23, with a ~4.5 GW development pipeline over the next five years) is driving demand for servers, storage, networking, power-management and cooling infrastructure.
- Global and Indian semiconductor demand growth driven by AI-native infrastructure, hyperscale/cloud expansion, embedded/edge applications and supply-chain diversification is expected to increase distribution and technical-design-support opportunities.
- India's IT spending is projected to reach USD176.3 billion in 2026 (+10.6% YoY), with device spending forecast to rise 9.9% to USD66.4 billion, supported by enterprise modernisation, replacement demand and AI-enabled technology adoption.
- Gaming market growth (Indian gaming market projected to grow from USD4.59bn in FY25 to USD5.37bn in FY26, at a longer-term CAGR of 15.62%) driven by esports, cloud/multiplayer gaming and premiumisation of gaming devices/peripherals.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Rashi Peripherals delivered 43% YoY revenue growth in Q3FY26 driven by 50% volume and 50% ASP growth due to global component shortages and preponed corporate buying ahead of price hikes, with PAT up 132% — this reflects structural demand for AI-ready PCs in India, amplified by policy tailwinds, and positions the company to sustain revenue growth even with flattish unit volumes through pricing power and distribution scale.
